elections.note: Marred by fraud; Aquino took office after the People Power Revolution

source.name: Wikipedia, citing the International Observer Delegation report (official Batasang Pambansa canvass)

elections.notes: The table is the official canvass by the Batasang Pambansa, which proclaimed Ferdinand Marcos the winner (53.62% per the infobox's COMELEC figures); he is flagged as winner on that basis. The lead says the election was marred by irregularities and fraud; NAMFREL's count (also in the article) had Corazon Aquino ahead with 7,909,320 votes to 7,376,599, and she was inaugurated on 25 February 1986 after the People Power Revolution deposed Marcos. 559,469 invalid ballots are excluded from the shares. Turnout is the infobox figure. The results come from the transcluded template "{{1986 Philippine presidential election results}}", cited here; the article is "1986 Philippine presidential election". Others: Reuben Canoy, Narciso Padilla. Region winners are from the article's by-region table of the official count; only Metro Manila, Bicol and the three Visayas regions had today's boundaries, so the other regions are left out.

source.name: Wikipedia, citing the Congress of the Philippines (national canvass)

elections.notes: Grace Poe ran as an independent (the table colours her as Partido Galing at Puso). Shares are of valid votes; 2,426,316 invalid ballots, which include 25,779 votes for Roy Señeres, who withdrew and died after the ballots were printed, are excluded. Turnout is the infobox figure. The results come from the transcluded template "{{2016 Philippine presidential election results}}", cited here; the article is "2016 Philippine presidential election". Region winners are the candidate with the most votes in each region, from the article's by-region table. Western and Central Visayas are left out: the table counts the Negros Island Region, which existed in 2016, separately. ARMM is matched to today's Bangsamoro region, whose boundaries differ slightly (Cotabato City joined it from Soccsksargen in 2019).
